commits.message:
feat(resume-builder): wire Summary AI Assistant and Align to Role to the real CORE/Hermes chain

Both screens rendered from static mock data with no backend calls
anywhere -- confirmed via a full audit earlier today (81 components
under resume-builder/, zero fetch/axios/useQuery calls). CORE's
resume-intelligence module (HERMES-800/HERMES-300 relay, built same
day) now has real frontend callers for two of its endpoints.

New: src/services/resume-intelligence.ts -- typed wrapper over
apiRequest() for summary/suggest, bullets/suggest, and match, mirroring
the existing chatwoot-support.ts service pattern.

SummarySectionEditor.tsx: all 5 "AI Writing Assistant" actions (Rewrite,
Improve ATS, Add Metrics, Missing Keywords, Tailor to Job) now call
suggestResumeSummary() with the user's actual draft summary and target
role, mapped to a per-action constraint string. Empty-draft and error
cases show a toast instead of silently failing. Suggestions still only
populate a preview panel -- apply/regenerate/dismiss unchanged, nothing
auto-writes over the user's summary.

BenchSalesCreateBaseResumeAlignRole.tsx + BenchSalesCreateBaseResumeModal.tsx:
this wizard had no real resume or job data in its state at all -- every
step rendered from disconnected mocks. Threaded real data through
instead of wiring the match call to fabricated input: resume skills/
work-authorization/location/experience now come from the same content
the Review Data step already displays (parsed from its skillGroups,
not duplicated new mock data), and required skills/years-experience
come from the actual Define Role form. Feeds a real matchResumeToJob()
call; the panel now renders the live match_score, decision, matched/
missing skills, and recommendation instead of a static three-bucket
mock. Per-experience "relevance" badges were dropped -- Hermes's
matching API doesn't return per-experience scores, so that badge was
invented UI with no backend counterpart.

Verified locally: `tsc --noEmit` clean across the project. Full browser
pass against a local mock of CORE's auth + resume-intelligence
responses (shaped from the live OpenAPI schema, not guessed) -- logged
in, opened the resume builder, ran "Rewrite Summary" and confirmed the
exact request payload (real summary text + real target role +
per-action constraint) and that "Apply" correctly wrote the suggestion
into the resume. Walked the full "Create Base Resume" wizard, selected
role tags Java/AWS/Salesforce against a consultant whose parsed skills
include Java/AWS but not Salesforce, and got back a real 67% match
score with Java+AWS correctly flagged relevant and Salesforce correctly
flagged missing.

Not done in this pass: live verification against the real deployed
CORE/Hermes chain -- the browser's CORS policy blocks a localhost dev
origin from the UAT backend (uat.jobfynder.com only allows
testing.jobfynder.com), so this used a local mock server instead. The
CORE-side chain itself was already verified live in an earlier commit
(scripts/verifyResumeIntelligence.mjs on jobFynder-BE-nestJS). Also not
touched: the "Generate with AI" panel (ResumeGenerateWithAi, shared by
Summary/Skills/Experience editors) -- still mock, separate change since
it has 3 call sites.

feat(resume-builder): wire Tier 1 -- Job Match, Skills validation, Experience bullets

Follow-up to the earlier Summary/Align-to-Role wiring. Scoped down from
the original Tier 1 list after checking each capability against Hermes's
live schema and CORE's actual routes -- two items turned out not to map
cleanly and were deliberately left alone rather than force-wired:

- Skills section: skills/normalize validates skills you already have
  against a taxonomy (canonical name, alias, unknown) -- it does not
  suggest new skills for a role. The existing "Suggest missing skills"/
  "Reorder by job relevance" mock actions and the Skills "Generate with
  AI" panel don't match what this endpoint does, so they stay mock.
  Added a new, honest "Validate Skills" action instead
  (SkillsSectionEditor.tsx): flags unrecognized skills and offers
  one-click canonical-name fixes (e.g. an alias -> its canonical form).

- ATS Check panel: not touched. Its "12 Parser Checks" (single-column
  layout, font compliance, special characters...), per-format export
  scores, and 51-ATS-system simulation are all document-rendering
  properties -- Hermes's quality/analyze works on text/structured data
  and cannot see a resume's actual formatting, so none of it can be
  wired without fabricating results. Flagging for a separate product
  conversation rather than wiring a fake score.

Wired for real, using capabilities that already exist:

- Job Match panel (ResumeJobMatchPanel.tsx): pasting a JD now calls
  CORE's existing POST /jobs/parse (built for the job-posting flow,
  reused here -- it already extracts structured skills from raw JD
  text via Hermes Understanding) to get real required skills, then
  POST /resume-intelligence/match for a real score and skill-gap
  breakdown. "Job-Specific Summary" now calls summary/suggest with the
  resume's real text and the parsed job title. "Best Variant ranking"
  and "Save Targeted Version" are left mock -- both need resume-variant
  persistence that doesn't exist anywhere yet (a separate, larger
  gap). Threaded `data` (ConsultantResumeData) down from
  ResumeBuilderPreviewPane, which wasn't passing it to this panel or
  to ResumeATSCheckPanel before.

- Experience section (ExperienceSectionEditor.tsx): "Generate with AI"
  now calls bullets/suggest with the role's existing bullets (or
  summary) as source_text and the resume's skills to emphasize,
  appending one new AI-suggested bullet instead of overwriting with a
  static 3-bullet mock block.

- ResumeGenerateWithAi.tsx (shared "Generate with AI" panel, used by
  Summary/Skills/Experience): added an optional `onGenerate` async
  prop as an alternative to the static `generatedContent` prop, so a
  real backend call can drive the same UI. Only Experience uses it in
  this pass -- Summary and Skills keep their existing static-mock
  prop, backward compatible with no behavior change for those two.

New: src/utils/resume-builder-document.ts -- buildResumeSourceText()
and buildResumeMatchInput(), shared plain-text/match-payload builders
from ConsultantResumeData, used by the Job Match panel (and available
for other panels that need the same resume-to-text serialization).

New service functions in resume-intelligence.ts: normalizeResumeSkills,
analyzeResumeQuality (added, not yet wired to any screen -- see ATS
Check note above), tailorResumeToJob (added, not yet wired -- Tailor to
Job screens are a separate follow-up), parseJobDescription (hits
/api/jobs/parse, not a /resume-intelligence/* route).

Verified locally: `tsc --noEmit` clean. Full browser pass against a
local mock of CORE's responses (shaped from Hermes's live OpenAPI
schema) -- confirmed real request payloads at each step (Validate
Skills sent all 18 actual skills; Job Match's parse-then-match chain
fired in the right order with the parsed job's real skills feeding the
match call; Job-Specific Summary carried the resume's real text and
the parsed job title; Experience's Generate call carried the role's
real existing bullets and the resume's real skill list) and correct
rendering/apply behavior for each.

Also found while checking the CORE side: a developer (atultiwari)
merged a substantial "Hermes core integration" refactor into main
today, replacing the resume-intelligence module built yesterday with a
proper HermesClient/HermesIntelligenceService architecture (retries,
typed errors, DTOs) and adding /jobs/parse, feedback/analyze, and a
prompt-based generateResumeSection() capability CORE already has but
nothing on the frontend calls yet. No CORE changes were needed for
this PR -- everything here uses routes that already exist.

feat(resume-builder): wire Tailor to Job (2 of its 3 screens) to real HERMES-300 tailoring

Closes out the Tier 1 list. Checked all three "Tailor to Job" surfaces
before touching anything -- one turned out not to be a tailoring
feature at all:

- ats-optimizer/ATSTailorPreviewSection.tsx: not touched. It's a static
  ATS-system browser with a "View All" nav link, no analysis action of
  any kind. Not part of this wiring.

Wired for real, using CORE's existing /jobs/parse + /resume-intelligence/tailor
(no backend changes needed):

- consultant/tailor-to-job/ConsultantTailorToJobSession.tsx: the
  "Job Targeting Engine" sub-section's "Analyze & Target" now parses
  the pasted JD via /jobs/parse and calls tailor with the consultant's
  real resume data, rendering a real match score, skill gap, and
  detected job title. "Job-Specific Summary" now generates a real
  summary via summary/suggest. Required threading `data`
  (ConsultantResumeData) down through ConsultantResumeBuilder ->
  ConsultantTailorToJobView -> Session, which wasn't passed before.

  Left untouched, same reasoning as the ATS Check panel decision
  earlier: the top "session created" banner, ATS Diagnostic, Strength
  Meters, Keyword Gaps (JD-term-frequency counts), Risk Factors,
  Benchmark vs Hired Profiles, and the whole ATS Optimization Engine
  sub-section. These are either document-rendering properties no
  text-analysis API can see, or specific statistical claims
  ("1,400+ similar role outcomes", "1,200 hired profiles") with no
  model or dataset behind them anywhere in this codebase -- wiring them
  would mean fabricating numbers, not connecting a real capability.
  "Best Variant for This Job" and "Save Targeted Version" also stay
  mock (same resume-variant-persistence gap noted for the Job Match
  panel).

- bench-sales/BenchSalesTailorResumeToJobModal.tsx: previously just
  showed a success toast on submit with no result of any kind. Now
  parses the JD, calls tailor, and renders the real match score,
  matched/missing skills, and opportunities. Used from both the
  bench-sales dashboard and the consultant's own "My Resumes" list,
  neither of which has a real per-item resume data source (no skills
  field exists on a consultant row or resume-list entry) -- reused the
  same Review Data snapshot already used for "Align to Role" as the
  resume-side input, same reasoning as that earlier decision: it's the
  only place in the app with real extracted resume content to point
  at, and it's disclosed as such in the new shared util below.

New: src/utils/resume-builder-bench-sales-review.ts -- extracted
getReviewedResumeSnapshot() out of BenchSalesCreateBaseResumeModal.tsx
(where it was previously a private, non-exported function only used
for Align to Role) into a shared util, since this pass needed the same
snapshot from a second, unrelated component. BenchSalesCreateBaseResumeModal.tsx
now imports it instead of duplicating it.

Verified locally: `tsc --noEmit` clean. Full browser pass against the
same local mock server (extended with a /resume-intelligence/tailor
handler) -- confirmed the real jobs/parse -> tailor chain fires in
order for both screens, with real resume skills/company/role in the
request and correct match-score/skill-gap/opportunities rendering in
both the bench-sales modal and the consultant tailoring session.

feat(resume-builder): redesign ATS Check around what quality/analyze can actually measure

Closes the one Tier 1 item left pending. This panel previously claimed
things no text-analysis API can determine: 12 "Parser Checks" (single-
column layout, font compliance, bullet-character parsing -- all
document-rendering properties Hermes can't see from text), per-format
export scores (PDF 92/DOCX 87/TXT 78, invented), and a 51-vendor ATS
simulation with individual per-system scores (Greenhouse 94%, Workday
81%, etc. -- no such simulation exists anywhere). None of it mapped to
quality/analyze's real output, so wiring it as-is would have meant
fabricating numbers under real-looking labels.

Rebuilt around what the endpoint actually returns:
- Top scores are now the real quality_score / completeness_score /
  provenance_score from Hermes, not a fabricated "ATS Compatibility
  Score".
- "Quality Metrics" replaces "Parser-Safe Validation (12 checks)" --
  renders Hermes's real per-metric code/label/score/status/message
  array instead of a hardcoded list of formatting claims.
- Missing/empty sections are now surfaced from the real response
  instead of assumed.
- Dropped entirely: Export Health Check (per-format scores) and the
  51-system ATS Parsing Simulation -- no capability backs either one.
- Kept the "Tailor Resume for Specific ATS" section (renamed "ATS
  Formatting Reference") -- it's generic, non-personalized formatting
  tips for named ATS systems, not a fabricated per-user score, so it
  doesn't have the same honesty problem as the rest of the panel.

Runs the real analyze call automatically when the tab opens (was
previously instant/static content -- now genuinely async, with
loading and error states).

Required threading `data` (ConsultantResumeData) into this component,
which previously rendered with zero props.

Verified locally: `tsc --noEmit` clean. Browser pass against the mock
server (extended with a quality/analyze handler) confirms the real
request fires on tab open and the panel renders whatever the response
says, including a deliberately-triggered missing-section flag --
proving it reflects the actual API response rather than a fixed
layout.

feat(resume-builder): wire the resume builder to real backend persistence

The foundation piece for everything in the "Tier 2" gap list (variants,
blind resume, collaboration, approval workflow all assume a real saved
resume exists somewhere). Before this, the entire resume builder only
ever saved to localStorage -- every "My Resumes" list, every score,
every consultant record was a client-only draft that vanished with the
browser storage.

Found CORE already has a complete Resume CRUD backend
(list/get/create-via-upload/update/delete, backed by a real `resumes`
Postgres table) that the frontend never called. See the companion
jobFynder-BE-nestJS PR ("Fix missing auth guard on /resume CRUD + add
JSON create endpoint") for what had to change there first: every one
of those routes was missing its auth guard entirely (would throw on
req.user for any real caller -- never caught because nothing called
them), and there was no way to create a resume from typed-in JSON
(only the file-upload-then-parse path existed).

New: src/services/resume.ts -- typed client for list/get/create/update/
delete, matching the backend's actual (intentionally per-endpoint
inconsistent) response shapes exactly rather than assuming a uniform
envelope.

New in src/utils/resume-builder-document.ts: toResumeWritePayload() /
fromResumeRecord() -- the mapping between ConsultantResumeData and
what CORE persists. Fields with no dedicated DB column (location,
links, work authorization, market preferences, skill categories) round-
trip through the new Resume.builderMetadata JSON column added in the
backend PR.

Rewired the whole loop:
- ConsultantMyResumesView.tsx: the resume list was three hardcoded
  mock cards with fabricated scores/statuses/variant-counts that had
  no connection to anything -- clicking "Open resume builder" on any
  of the three opened the exact same single localStorage-backed
  builder regardless of which was clicked. Now lists real resumes via
  listResumes(), "New" creates a real resume and opens it, each card
  opens its own real resume by id, delete actually deletes. Dropped
  the fabricated per-resume score/status/tag/variant-count -- no real
  source for any of them yet (score needs a quality/analyze call per
  resume, status/variants need the not-yet-built Variants feature).
  Also stopped this view's "New" button from opening
  BenchSalesCreateResumeVariantModal, which was wired to a hardcoded
  mock consultant unrelated to the logged-in user -- wrong flow for
  "create my own resume".
- ConsultantResumeBuilder.tsx: takes a `resumeId` prop now, loads the
  real record on mount, autosaves via PUT on a 1s debounce (falls back
  to POST if somehow opened without an id). Removed localStorage
  entirely -- the server is the only source of truth now.
- ConsultantResumeBuilderNav.tsx: the "Saved" indicator was always a
  static green dot regardless of what was actually happening. Now
  reflects real saveState (saving / saved / error) from the autosave
  above.
- ResumeBuilder.tsx (page): threads the selected resumeId from the
  list view into the builder.

Verified locally: `tsc --noEmit` clean. Full browser pass against a
mock server extended with an in-memory /resume CRUD store -- created a
resume, edited the headline, confirmed the real PUT fired with the
exact edited value and the full real payload (skills/experience/
education/certifications/builderMetadata), navigated back and
confirmed the list re-fetched from the server and showed the saved
title and date, then deleted it and confirmed the list returned to
empty. Not yet verified against the live database -- blocked on the
companion backend PR's migration being deployed first.

feat(resume-builder): wire Resume Variants to real create/list/duplicate

Second piece on top of the resume-persistence commit. Depends on the
companion jobFynder-BE-nestJS PR's second commit ("add resume variants
(label, variantType, parentResumeId)").

- ConsultantResumeVariantsView.tsx: took a `baseResumeId` prop (the
  currently open resume) instead of rendering a static list of 3 mock
  variant cards. Lists real variants via listResumeVariants(), creates
  via the modal below, duplicates via createResumeVariant() with a
  "Copy of X" label. Dropped the fabricated per-variant ATS/Match
  scores -- same reasoning as the ATS Check and Job Match panel calls
  earlier: no real per-variant score exists (that would need a
  quality/analyze + match call per variant, not built here), so showing
  invented numbers next to a real label/type/role would be worse than
  not showing a score at all.
- ConsultantCreateResumeVariantModal.tsx: now actually creates a
  variant instead of just showing a success toast. Removed the "Base
  From" dropdown -- it let you pick among mock variants as a base, but
  there's only one real base resume in scope here (the one currently
  open), so the field had no real options to offer. A variant of a
  variant is a real future need, just not built in this pass.
- ConsultantResumeBuilder.tsx: passes the open resume's id down as
  `baseResumeId`.

Not wired in this pass: BenchSalesCreateResumeVariantModal.tsx and
BenchSalesGenerateBlindResumeModal.tsx (the bench-sales dashboard's
variant/blind-resume actions on OTHER consultants' resumes). Checked
before starting -- CORE's /resume routes are ownership-scoped to
`req.user._id` by design, so a bench-sales user cannot create/read/
write a resume owned by a different consultant with the current auth
model. Wiring those two screens for real would mean either bypassing
that check (a real security bug) or building a proper delegated-access
model first (an org/assignment-based permission layer -- there's a
ConsultantAssignment table in the schema that looks like the right
foundation for it, not yet explored). Flagging rather than building
around the gap.

Verified locally: `tsc --noEmit` clean. Browser pass against the mock
server (extended with in-memory /resume/:id/variants handlers) --
created a variant with a real label/type/target-role, confirmed it
rendered correctly, then duplicated it and confirmed a second real
variant appeared with the correct "Copy of ..." label. Not verified
against the live database -- same blocker as the first commit.

feat(resume-builder): wire Feedback's AI Analysis to real feedback/analyze

CORE already had a real /resume-intelligence/feedback/analyze route
(built during the earlier "hermes-core-integration" merge) that
nothing on the frontend called yet. Checked the schemas before writing
any code: Hermes's HermesResumeFeedbackItem
(title/current/suggested_improvement/why_it_matters/severity/category)
maps almost field-for-field onto the FE's existing FeedbackItem type
(title/currentText/suggestedText/whyItMatters/severity/issueType) --
this screen was clearly designed against this exact capability, it
just never got connected.

ConsultantFeedbackView.tsx: runs a real analysis on mount using the
resume's actual text, replacing the 4 hardcoded "ai_analysis" mock
items with whatever Hermes actually returns. "Apply Suggestion" now
writes the real suggested text into the resume's summary when the
feedback item is summary-related (via a new onApplySummarySuggestion
callback from ConsultantResumeBuilder); for other sections it shows an
honest "update this section manually" note instead of a no-op, since
automatically rewriting skills/experience/education from a feedback
item isn't safely generic the way summary replacement is.

Dropped the 3 mock items sourced from "tech_recruiter", "bench_sales",
and "service_provider" -- there's no comment-thread or marketplace
backend behind any of them (a real recruiter leaving feedback on a
specific consultant's resume needs a persistence + notification layer
that doesn't exist yet), so showing fabricated recruiter feedback next
to real AI feedback would blur which one is genuine. The tab/filter
UI for those sources stays in place for when that capability exists;
"Add Feedback" (a human manually typing in a note during this session)
and "Endorse Skills" are untouched -- they're real local actions, just
not yet persisted anywhere, which is a different, smaller gap than
fabricated content.

New in resume-intelligence.ts: analyzeResumeFeedback(), typed against
Hermes's live HermesResumeFeedbackItem schema (not guessed).

Verified locally: `tsc --noEmit` clean. Browser pass against the mock
server (extended with a feedback/analyze handler returning two
distinct items, one summary-related and one skills-related) --
confirmed the real request fired on mount, both items rendered with
their real title/section/severity/suggestion text, and clicking
"Apply Suggestion" on the summary item actually overwrote the resume's
Professional Summary with the exact suggested text.

feat(resume-builder): wire Performance Insights to real submission history

Depends on the companion jobFynder-BE-nestJS PR's third commit
("add GET /bench/submissions/mine"). Closes out this pass of Tier 2
with no leftover mock data in this screen -- every number shown is
computed from real submissions, or the section is removed/replaced
with an honest empty state when there's no real capability behind it.

What was fabricated before and is now either real or gone:
- "Total Submissions / Shortlisted / Interviews / Placements /
  Marketability Score" summary cards: now 4 real counts computed from
  actual submission statuses (In Screening replaces Shortlisted --
  SCREENING is a real status, "shortlisted" isn't). Marketability
  Score dropped entirely -- there was never a real formula behind it,
  just a hardcoded 56.
- Weekly trend chart: was 3 fabricated percentage series (reply/
  shortlist/interview rate) with no underlying events to compute them
  from. Replaced with a single real series -- actual submission count
  per week, grouped from real submissionDate values. Rewrote
  PerformanceWeeklyTrendChart.tsx to match (single series instead of
  three).
- Per-variant performance cards: dropped "Marketability Score" and
  the reply/shortlist/interview/conversion-rate quad-stat (all
  fabricated percentages), replaced with a real funnel (submitted /
  interview / placed counts) built from submissions whose
  resumeVersionId matches one of the user's real resumes or variants.
  Rewrote PerformanceVariantCard.tsx accordingly. Cards only render
  for resumes that actually have a linked submission; if none do
  (resumeVersionId isn't populated by the current bench-sales
  submission flow yet), shows one honest note instead of 3 empty mock
  cards.
- "AI Recommendations" (3 generic bullet points, no model behind any
  of them) dropped entirely. Replaced with one factually-derived
  check: submissions still in "Submitted" status after 14+ days,
  computed from real dates -- not a comparison to an "average" that
  doesn't exist anywhere in this codebase.
- Recent Application Activity: now the actual most recent submissions
  (job title, client, status, date), not a hardcoded list.
- "Sync Job Tracker" (previously just a success toast, no actual
  sync): replaced with "Refresh", which actually refetches.
- "Track Outcome" button/modal: removed from this screen entirely,
  not just left as a no-op. A consultant has no legitimate way to
  write to Submission.status -- only the recruiter who filed it can
  (checked in submission.service.ts), and status changes carry real
  commission/placement implications. Leaving a "Track Outcome" button
  next to now-real data would imply it writes to the system of
  record when it can't and shouldn't. ConsultantTrackOutcomeModal.tsx
  itself is untouched (not deleted) in case it's reused elsewhere;
  just stopped rendering it from this view.

New: src/services/bench-submissions.ts -- typed client for the new
endpoint.

Verified locally: `tsc --noEmit` clean. Browser pass against the mock
server (extended with a submissions/mine handler returning 3
submissions -- one INTERVIEW, one PLACED both linked to a real created
resume, one 20-day-old SUBMITTED unlinked) -- confirmed all 4 summary
counts, the weekly trend chart, the per-resume funnel card (2
submissions, 1 placed), the stale-submission warning, and the recent
activity list all matched the real input data exactly.
